images.title: Split or meet?
images.purpose: Contrast the two kinds of story: cutting into equal pieces needs the HCF, and events lining up again needs the LCM.
images.composition: Two halves side by side separated by a thin grey vertical line: ribbons cut into equal pieces on the left, a number line with two sets of rings on the right, white space around each.
exact_structure: Left half, heading Split: HCF in reddish purple #CC79A7.
Under it, a teal #0072B2 ribbon labelled 24 m cut by grey #6B7280 dashed lines into exactly 2 equal pieces.
Below it, an amber #E69F00 ribbon labelled 36 m, 1.5 times as long, cut into exactly 3 equal pieces the same length as the teal pieces.
One piece outlined in reddish purple with the label 12 m.
Right half, heading Meet: LCM in green #009E73.
A grey number line from 0 to 36 with ticks labelled 0, 12, 18, 24, 36 only.
Teal dots above the line at 12, 24 and 36 (exactly 3); amber dots below the line at 18 and 36 (exactly 2).
A green ring around 36 where a teal and an amber dot meet.
rejection: ribbon pieces of unequal length, or a count other than 2 teal and 3 amber pieces
teal dots at places other than 12, 24, 36 or amber dots at places other than 18, 36
images.takeaway: Equal pieces with nothing left point to the HCF; things happening together again point to the LCM.
images.description: Left, ribbons of 24 m and 36 m cut into 12 m pieces under Split: HCF; right, a number line where steps of 12 and 18 meet at 36 under Meet: LCM.
images.context: Shown beside the concept text and video on choosing HCF or LCM.
images.teaching_notes: Ask which half each new story looks like before computing anything.

image_decisions.why: Placing the two story types side by side is the clearest way to see which value each one needs.
